extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators who have received an ERC main grant (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced or Synergy) preparing an ERC Proof of Concept (PoC) application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/evaluation rules for preparing and submitting an ERC Proof of Concept (PoC) grant application to explore commercial or societal potential of an ERC-funded research idea. Covers who can apply, host institution requirements, required documents, ethics review, eligible activities, funding, and the evaluation/scoring framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Principal Investigator and linkage to ERC main grant
rubrics_metrics.description: All Principal Investigators in one of the ERC frontier research main grants (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced or Synergy) are eligible. Principal Investigators in an ongoing main grant, or Principal Investigators in a main grant that has ended after 1 January 2025, are eligible to apply. The Principal Investigator must be able to demonstrate the relation between the idea to be taken to proof of concept and the ERC frontier research project in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PoC funding is made available only to those who already have an ERC award to establish proof of concept of an idea that was generated in the course of their ERC-funded projects. Proposals must draw substantially on their ERC funded research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on submissions and per-project limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A Principal Investigator may submit only one application per call. A maximum of three Proof of Concept Grants may be awarded per main grant project, except for Synergy Grant, in which case a maximum of six Proof of Concept Grants may be awarded per ERC funded project. Synergy Grant Principal Investigators are eligible to apply only with the written consent of all Principal Investigators in the same Synergy Grant project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should track how many PoC grants have already been awarded to their main grant and obtain required consents for Synergy projects before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution (HI) eligibility and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Host Institution must engage the Principal Investigator for at least the duration of the Proof of Concept project. The Host Institution must either be established in an EU Member State or associated country (AC) as a legal entity created under national law, or it may be an International European Interest Organisation (such as CERN, EMBL, etc.), the European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) or any other entity created under EU law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International organisations with headquarters in an EU Member State or AC will be deemed established in that Member State/AC. Any type of legal entity, public or private, including universities, research organisations and undertakings can host PIs and their teams. The PI can submit the PoC proposal with a different HI than the one where the ERC main grant was implemented, provided that this other HI complies with the eligibility criteria described in the Work Programme. A Host Institution binding statement of support is a required supplementary document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding: lump sum and project duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Work Programme 2026 will continue to award Proof of Concept Grants on the basis of a lump sum of EUR 150,000 for a period of 18 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget planning and proposed activities should be realistic and feasible within the lump sum and 18-month timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness — required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ERC Proof of Concept grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative form, the proposal (part B) and the supplementary documents (Host Institution binding statement of support and if applicable ethics self-assessment, additional ethics documentation and letters of support or intent from the relevant stakeholders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the completed proposal by the specified submission deadline of the chosen call. Missing required documents may render an application incomplete/ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be submitted at any time from the opening date of the chosen call until the specified submission deadline. As of 2024, applications to the Proof of Concept Grant will be evaluated and selected in two instead of three rounds, based on two specific cut-off dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the published calls, cut-off dates and deadlines on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and the Official Journal. Plan submissions to meet the chosen call's cut-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review — requirement and legal basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal that is selected for funding must undergo an ethics review. This is a legal requirement under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme - Regulation 2021/695: Eligible actions and ethical principles (Article 18) and Ethics (Article 19). The basis for this ethics review is Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table – EIT – and the Ethics Self-Assessment – ESA) and Part B of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-detailed ESA is crucial to facilitate the process as it clarifies what issues are linked to the proposed research activities and how these will be dealt with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review process and stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethics review comprises 3 stages: Ethics pre-screening (performed internally by ERCEA staff to clear proposals without ethics issues or with simple ethics issues), Ethics screening (panels of independent ethics reviewers identifying proposals with potentially serious and/or complex ethics issues), and Ethics assessment (panels of independent ethics reviewers discussing the serious and/or complex ethics issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearance of proposals with non-serious/complex issues may include observations and references to documents to be kept on file. After screening, applicants might be contacted (typically one week after the screening panel) and are given 3 weeks to reply. Ethics deliverables may be formulated if follow-up is needed during project implementation. Research involving human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) requires all ethics review steps and a specific EC approval following consultation to the HE programme committee (comitology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sole criterion: Excellence — Breakthrough innovation potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakthrough innovation potential: Proposals will have to demonstrate that the proposed Proof of Concept activity has the potential to drive innovation and business inventiveness and/or tackle societal challenges, and that the proposed expected outcomes are innovative or distinctive compared to existing solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the PoC activity will lead to distinctive/innovative outcomes compared to current solutions, and how it could drive commercialization or societal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sole criterion: Excellence — Approach and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach and methodology: The proposed Proof of Concept activities and planning are feasible within the proposed timescales and resources, and are appropriate and effective to explore the pathway from ground-breaking research towards innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a feasible, well-structured workplan with appropriate methods, milestones, feasibility justification, and resource allocation for the 18-month PoC period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sole criterion: Excellence — Principal Investigator (strategic lead & project management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigator - strategic lead and project management: The Principal Investigator needs to demonstrate a clear vision on how to organise the management of the project, the consolidation of information and data needed to take strategic decisions and implement the proposed plan, including risk and contingency measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe PI's strategic role, management arrangements, decision-making processes, risk identification and mitigation, and capacity to lead translation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring procedure, pass thresholds and Seal of Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: External independent experts will evaluate each admissible and eligible proposal and mark it as 'very good', 'good' or 'fail' for each of the three evaluation elements. In order to be considered for funding, proposals will have to be awarded a pass mark ('very good' or 'good') by a majority of the experts on each of the three evaluation elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that receive a pass mark in all three evaluation elements but cannot be funded due to lack of budget may be awarded a 'Seal of Excellence'. Holders of a Seal of Excellence are directed to national/regional support programmes and National Contact Points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project purpose and eligible Proof of Concept activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of Concept Grants aim at maximising the value of the excellent research that the ERC funds by funding further work (activities which were not scheduled to be funded by the original ERC frontier research grant) to verify the innovation potential of ideas arising from ERC funded projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of funded activities include: testing, experimenting, demonstrating and validating the idea; conducting research required to address weaknesses uncovered by these activities; establishing viability, technical issues and overall direction; clarifying IPR protection or knowledge transfer strategy; involving industrial partners, societal or cultural organisations, policymakers or other stakeholders; assessing potential end users of the expected innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and evaluation procedure: single-stage/single-step
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of Concept calls have a single-stage submission and single-step evaluation procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no multi-stage selection; the full proposal is evaluated by external experts at once against the three excellence elements.
